milestones.note: Earliest commit carrying a Claude Code, OpenCode or Codex attribution trailer. Unattributed agent commits before it cannot be told apart.
First AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md added to any repository.
First SKILL.md added to any repository.
First package.json gaining a single "verify" script.
First ESLint config commit whose message says it hardens or tightens lint. Only one repository's history says so in words.
ibni's predecessor, the implementation-workspace CLI, first committed.
The worktree CLI renamed ibni and split into commands.
Each workspace gets a block of ports.
Setup and verify wait for a machine-wide run slot.

Renamed to mexxi with a docs site and one-paste setup; GitHub Pages first deployed the same day. The MIT licence followed on 2026-10-23. GitHub does not record when the repository's visibility changed.

eras.note: Instructions in prose; per-repository verify scripts appear.
Verify runs through verifika, which keeps check output out of the agent's context.
ibni, one config file, mexxi public.
Port blocks, run slots and systemd scopes.

hypotheses.headline: Always-loaded rules across repositories: peak 96 (2026-10-25), now 96. Workflow prose in project repositories: peak 118 rules (2026-08-23), now 23. mexxi's own workflow prose: peak 106 (2026-09-30), now 97. Tool-enforced concerns across repositories: 1 at the first snapshot, 25 now.

comparisons.metric: workflow prose rules kept in project repositories

caveats: Counts directive lines (always, never, must, prefer...) in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and rule files, and separately in commands and agent definitions; it does not weigh how long or how often a rule is read.
Global instructions live in mexxi's own AGENTS.md since August 2026; earlier global files in the hosts' own config directories were not in Git and have no history.
New repositories joining raise the total without any one backpack growing.

hypotheses.headline: Claims that checks pass with no passing check after the last edit: 11.5% of 26 claims (16 sessions) before each repository added its verify script, 8.7% of 1338 claims (301 sessions) after. The detector's precision was 28-48% on a hand-checked sample, so this cannot carry a verdict.
caveats: Session logs start on 2026-08-20; the first verify script is dated 2026-08-24. The 'before' side is the few sessions in repositories that added theirs later.
A hand-checked sample of 25 flagged claims found 7 clearly unverified, 5 ambiguous and 13 false positives (METHOD.md).
Checks run by delegated subagents are invisible to the parent session and read as unverified.

hypotheses.headline: Only 1 repository's history dates a lint tightening in words (2026-08-23). That repository has 0 sessions before the date and 78 after, so there is no before to compare.
caveats: Corrections are counted with the retro's CORRECTION_RE; it does not know which pattern a correction is about, so 'the same pattern' cannot be tested from transcripts.
Lint strictness over time is shown as the number of rules set to error in each ESLint config (backpack rows, lintErrorRules).

hypotheses.headline: Median check-run output went from 513 to 372 bytes (p90 6038 to 1782); compactions per session 0.15 to 0.49. Claude Code only: p90 2310 to 1782 bytes, compactions 0.07 to 0.49 per session (56 and 72 sessions).

comparisons.metric: median bytes per check run, Claude Code only
p90 bytes per check run, Claude Code only
compactions per session, Claude Code only

caveats: Before verifika most sessions ran in OpenCode, after it all ran in Claude Code: the host, its compaction policy and the models changed at the same time. The Claude Code-only rows hold the host constant.
Agents often pipe check output through tail or grep, so bytes per check run measure what reached the context, not what the check printed.

hypotheses.headline: 5.7% of 2731 failed Bash calls had an environmental cause (shell glob, timeout, busy port, missing package or command). Most failures were the checks themselves failing, which is the work, not friction. Separately, 392 glob aborts and 422 hidden exit codes hit calls that often reported success.
caveats: Failures matching no pattern are not proof of model error: most are failing tests and builds during normal work.
Model intelligence is not measured; only environmental causes can be recognised from output text.

hypotheses.headline: Mean daily peak of concurrent sessions: 1.63 before ibni, 2.14 after. Port clashes per 100 tool calls: 0.08 before port blocks, 0.14 after; timeouts 0.03 to 0.

comparisons.metric: mean daily peak of concurrent sessions
port clashes per 100 tool calls, Claude Code only
timeouts per 100 tool calls, Claude Code only

caveats: The port-block 'after' side covers 3 days (2026-10-25 to 2026-10-27).
Concurrency counts sessions with activity within 30 minutes of each other; an idle open session does not count.

notes: constitutionofmalta.com: no repository by that name exists locally or on GitHub; alexportelli12/constitution-explained (public, July 2025, with CLAUDE.md and .claude/) is taken to be it.
coding-agent-config is mexxi's earlier name: GitHub redirects it to alexportelli12/mexxi, so its history is mexxi's history.
Codex: only start, end, place and tool-call counts are read (five sessions), so Codex sessions count toward coverage and concurrency only.
Claude Code keeps transcripts for cleanupPeriodDays (90 here), but the oldest transcript on disk starts on 2026-09-26; nothing older survives to measure.
Session metrics before 2026-08-20 do not exist: anything older comes from Git history only.
Sessions whose working directory is under /tmp (segwi canaries, test fixtures) are excluded; their counts are in coverage.excluded.
Repositories not listed for publication are labelled 'private repo A', 'B'... in order of their first commit.
